motion.name: settle
motion.value: 0.9s ease-settle both; from opacity 0, translate 0 28px, blur 10px; staggered 80ms (140ms between calendar slabs)

motion.name: drift
motion.value: linear, scroll-driven; translate 0 var(--drift); hero planes -120px / -160px / -200px over 0 to 120vh, field shapes -36px over their view timeline
motion.purpose: Depth planes: nearer glass moves more.

motion.name: scene-change
motion.value: 500ms to 700ms ease-settle on opacity, translate, filter

motion.name: scene-duration

motion.name: reduced-motion

narrative.overview:
Every booking is a slab of tinted glass, and where two slabs overlap the colour deepens to violet. The double booking is visible before any text explains it, and the whole system is built outward from that one picture: the mark is two overlapping arches, the page furniture is large glass arches, pills and rounded tiles, and the product itself is shown on white panels that float over a field of a single glass colour.

The ground is a pale mineral grey-green with near-black ink. Pages are light, airy and centred, with long vertical pauses between sections. Glass is decorative and sits behind content; the white panel is where reading happens. The system has two registers: a persuading register (glass, fields, panels, motion) and a reading register (ground, ink and hairlines only, used for limits, guides and comparisons).

Dark mode is its own set of values, not an inversion: the ground goes near-black, the glass colours brighten, the overlap becomes a light violet, and glass stops multiplying with what is beneath it.

The dashboard under `src/app/(app)` is outside this system. It uses the monochrome `:root` tokens at the top of `src/app/globals.css` (white ground, Geist only, colour reserved for booking sources and states). The two worlds share the token names, the three source colours' meaning, and the mark, which the dashboard draws in a single ink tone.
keyCharacteristics: Tinted glass shapes with grain, an inner highlight and a coloured cast shadow.
Three glass colours with fixed meaning; violet appears where two meet.
White product panels floating over a field of one glass colour.
Display type at regular weight, large and tightly tracked; never bold.
Pills for every control; no square buttons.
Slow, settling motion: glass drifts on scroll, nothing bounces.

rules.name: The Fixed Meaning Rule
rules.body: Coral is Airbnb, blue is Booking.com, green is a direct booking, on every surface and in the dashboard too. A glass colour is never chosen for variety when it sits next to product data.

rules.name: The Earned Violet Rule
rules.body: Violet is what two colours make together. Use it for a clash, for focus and selection, and as a field tint; never for a call to action. The primary action is ink.

rules.name: The Drawn Overlap Rule
rules.body: In light mode glass multiplies with what is under it; in dark mode it does not. The overlapping nights in the calendar are therefore drawn as their own violet block in both modes, never left to the blend.

rules.name: The Field Text Rule
rules.body: Paragraphs set directly on a field use ink mixed with the field's own colour (`color-mix(in oklab, ink 72%, field colour)`), which holds above 8:1; headings stay pure ink.

rules.name: The Regular Weight Rule
rules.body: Funnel Display is always set at 400. The one exception is the wordmark beside the mark, which is 500 at 19px. Emphasis in running text is Geist 500, never bold display.

rules.name: The Balanced Break Rule
rules.body: Headings use `text-wrap: balance` and lead paragraphs `text-wrap: pretty`, each with a character-width cap, so lines break by sense at every width.

rules.name: The Three Planes Rule
rules.body: Glass further away moves less. Decorative shapes drift upward on scroll at plane-specific distances (120px, 160px and 200px over the first 120vh in the hero; 36px inside a field), linearly, tied to scroll position. A far echo shape is blurred 2px at half opacity.

rules.name: The Settle Rule
rules.body: Things arrive by settling: 28px of rise, a 10px blur clearing, 0.9s on `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`, staggered 80ms apart. Controls respond in 200ms. Nothing bounces or overshoots. With reduced motion nothing drifts or plays, and the demo rests on the scene that shows the clash.

rules.name: The Material Rule
rules.body: Glass always carries grain (a soft-light noise layer) and a top highlight, so the colour reads as a material and not as a gradient.

dos: Do keep coral for Airbnb, blue for Booking.com and green for direct bookings wherever product data appears.
Do put product material on a white panel, and float that panel over a field of one glass colour.
Do give each panel one reading.
Do set Funnel Display at 400 and let size carry the hierarchy.
Do crop and rotate decorative glass, keep it behind content, and mark it `aria-hidden`.
Do use ink for the primary action and a white pill for the second.
Do drop to the reading register (ground, ink, hairlines) when the content is limits, steps or comparisons.
Do write the source's name beside its colour; colour never carries the meaning alone.
Do give dark mode its own values through the same token names.
donts: Don't use violet for a button or a link; it marks a clash, focus and selection.
Don't set display type in bold, or in capitals.
Don't put text on a decorative glass shape; only booking slabs carry labels.
Don't use flat colour blocks or plain gradients where glass is meant; glass has grain, a highlight and a cast shadow.
Don't add hard, offset or grey drop shadows; shadows are long, soft and coloured or ambient.
Don't use `faint` for sentences, or `muted` for a label on a booking slab.
Don't rely on the blend mode to show an overlap; draw it.
Don't add motion that bounces, loops for decoration, or ignores the reduced-motion preference.
Don't bring the `.brand` tokens into the dashboard, or the dashboard's bordered cards into the public pages.
